## Goal

A person shares into their organization from the machine they work on: one instance linked to their own home and to each organization's, with every command saying which home it means and none guessing.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| RM-11 | An owner instance links to several homes on one server, each link with its own grant, connection, cursor and relay mark. Sign-in, sharing and reads name the home, and nothing is shared into an organization's home by a default the person didn't see | I, C | `org-link.test.ts`: a home written by the released version upgrades its link, hosted artifacts and pending push; one instance holds a personal and an organization link on one server, each with its own connection, cursor and relay mark; the share rule's four cases; one artifact on two homes; `remote/login { org }` against the released server image fails and leaves no grant; the membership cases again through a person's own sign-in; the kit's `remote.organization` against both reference hosts |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- one link per server and home on the owner instance: the ledger's migration, credentials per link, and a connection, cursor and relay mark per link;
- `remote/login` with `org`, the guard against a server that predates organization homes, `remote/status` per link, `remote/instances` and revoking one;
- the share rule that never guesses a home, and sharing an artifact as private;
- the CLI: `login --org`, `logout` with `--org`, `--personal` or `--instance`, `share --cloud` with `--org`, `--personal` or `--private`, `access`, `status`;
- the conformance scenario `remote.organization`;
- the Skill and docs for sharing into an organization (prose with Mirza, D149).

Design detail for this package:

- D170 designed this package's surface (INTERFACES §18.10's owner side and commands). Build it as written; settle finer shapes under D123 and record them additively.
- **First, the two things that can corrupt.** (1) The ledger's migration 18, which gives `remote_link` a local key and re-keys `hosted_artifact`, `version_push`, `remote_missing` and `relayed_run`: prove it on a home written by the released version, with a link, hosted artifacts and a pending push. (2) The downgrade guard: `remote/login` with `org` against a server from before WP-33 must fail with `MOSTRA_REMOTE_HOME_UNKNOWN` and revoke the grant it was given, checked against the released image.
- **One link per server and home:** its own grant, refresh token, link ID, connection, follow cursor and relay mark. Credentials per link beside the existing file (the personal link keeps its file name). A sign-in rebinds a link only for the same account and home. `remote/status` answers one entry per link with its home and role.
- **The share rule:** the home named; else the only link on that server; else the home the artifact is already hosted on there; else `MOSTRA_REMOTE_HOME_AMBIGUOUS`, listing the choices. Calls that act on a hosted artifact take `hosted: { server?, org? }` to name one home when it is hosted on several.
- **Commands** (INTERFACES §18.7): `login --org [<handle>]`, `logout --org|--personal|--instance`, `share --cloud --org|--personal|--private`, `access`, and `status` listing every link. `remote/instances` and `remote/instance.revoke` forward to WP-33's `hosted/links` and `hosted/link.revoke`. Help text is prose for Mirza (D149).
- Repeat WP-33's membership, removal and suspension cases with instances signed in through `remote/login { org }`, so each rule is proven through a person's own sign-in as well as a key.
- The conformance kit gains `remote.organization`: its server loads a small operator module naming an organization with the host's signed-in person as a member; the host signs in with `org`, shares and receives the delivery.

## Out of scope

- Reads of artifacts the instance doesn't own, and adoption (WP-35)
- Any change to what the server decides: a defect found there is fixed with its own check and recorded

## Acceptance evidence

RM-11's check: a home written by the released version upgrades with its link, hosted artifacts and pending push intact; one instance holds a personal link and an organization's on one server, each with its own connection; the share rule's four cases; sign-in with `org` against the released server image fails and leaves no grant; WP-33's membership and removal cases repeated through a person's own sign-in; the kit's scenario against both reference hosts.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- The migration runs on every existing owner's ledger: it must be idempotent, keep every pending push, and leave a personal link exactly as it was.
- Nothing may ever be shared under an organization's name by a default: the ambiguity rule has a seed for each fallback.

## Handoff

A person links a machine to each of their homes and shares into the one they name. WP-35 lets members read each other's pages from the CLI and moves a page to another member's instance.
